title: Gini Impurity
statement: Implement `gini(labels)` for a non-empty list of integer class labels. Return 1 minus the sum of squared class proportions. A pure node, where every label is the same, has Gini impurity 0.

approaches.name: Frequency map
approaches.explanation: CART uses Gini because it is cheaper than entropy and similarly ranks splits.

editorial: Gini impurity G = 1 − Σₖ pₖ² is the probability that two labels drawn with replacement from the node disagree. CART decision trees pick the split that most reduces the weighted Gini of the children. Entropy ranks splits similarly but needs logarithms. A pure node has p = 1 for one class, so G = 0, and the tree can stop splitting there.
